subject: general
question: Select the correct pair from the following options based on the refractive defects of vision.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Myopia - near-sightedness and Hypermetropia - far-sightedness**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Myopia** is a refractive error where close objects are seen clearly, but distant objects appear blurry.
 
• **Hypermetropia** is a refractive error where distant objects are seen clearly, but close objects appear blurry.
 
• Myopia is commonly known as **near-sightedness** or short-sightedness.
 
• Hypermetropia is commonly known as **far-sightedness** or long-sightedness.
 
• Both conditions can be corrected using glasses, contact lenses, or refractive surgery.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Astigmatism**

 
 
• It is a common refractive error caused by an irregularly shaped cornea or lens.
 
• Both near and distant objects can appear blurry or distorted.
 
• Astigmatism can occur in combination with myopia or hypermetropia.
 
• It is typically corrected with glasses, contact lenses, or refractive surgery.
 
 
 
• **Presbyopia**
 
 
• Aging-related condition where the eye's lens loses flexibility, affecting the ability to focus on close objects.
 
• Commonly occurs in people over the age of 40.
 
• It is corrected using reading glasses or bifocals.
 
 
 
• **Corrective Lenses**
 
 
• Glasses and contact lenses are the most common methods for correcting refractive errors.
 
• They work by altering the path of light entering the eye to ensure it focuses correctly on the retina.
 
 
 
• **Refractive Surgery**
 
 
• Procedures like LASIK and PRK reshape the cornea to correct refractive errors.
 
• They provide a permanent solution but involve surgical risks and costs.
